keyQuestions.text: Q1. Which activation-manifest ownership model should be the long-term contract, and what breaks under authored-only, runtime-authoritative, or a better third model?
Q2. What exact mechanism makes authored closure tracing fail for `cli-external-orchestration` and `sk-design` while byte-identical runtime manifests resolve?
Q3. Where should compiled-route freshness block—pre-commit, pre-push, CI, or session hook—and how should legitimately uncompilable in-progress hubs escape?
Q4. Should staging and rollback remain for a single-operator git-backed build tool, given the former live-runtime `rmSync` hazard?
Q5. What is the minimum sequenced work for reproducibility, self-reporting, and unattended safety, split into work safe now versus work that must wait for `sk-design`?

keyFindings.summary: Closure fails via resolveRoute null from live snapshot compile errors / identity bind; not manifest bytes
Block freshness in CI; allowlist only inputs-do-not-compile
Retain staging/rename/rollback; never restore live rmSync
Fix cli harness + dual write-back + CI now; wait on sk-design remint

ruledOutDirections: manifest-byte comparison as Q2 root cause
baselineContradictions: Runtime resolution currently fails for cli-external-orchestration and sk-design
sk-design authored vs runtime manifests currently differ
